visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video begins with a white screen displaying a scientific journal article from 'Proceedings B' titled 'Ancient DNA and biomarkers from archaeological artifacts'. Yellow text overlays appear at the top. The background is a digital screenshot of a website. (2) A man with short black hair and glasses, wearing a black high-neck long-sleeve shirt, appears in a medium shot. He stands in front of a snowy park background with trees and a white structure that resembles a snowman. He gestures with his hands while speaking directly to the camera. (3) A split-screen graphic appears; the left side shows a topographic map of the Alpine region with color-coded markers, and the right side shows close-up photos of dark, lumpy resin fragments and pottery shards. The man remains visible in a small circular inset at the bottom. (4) The man returns to full-screen medium shot against the snowy park background. He continues speaking with animated facial expressions and hand movements, emphasizing points. (5) A detailed scientific chart showing DNA presence of various animals and plants (Animallia, Plantae) appears. The chart uses colored dots on a grid. The man remains in a small inset. (6) The man returns to the center of the frame, holding a small dark object (representing the 'gum') and pointing at the screen. He mimics the action of chewing. (7) A bar chart titled 'Genetic sex' appears, showing frequency distributions of XX and XY chromosomes across different artifact types like 'Pieces', 'Hafting', and 'Repair'. The colors are green, orange, and beige. (8) The man concludes the video in the snowy park, gesturing widely with both hands, his mouth moving rapidly as he delivers the final remarks. A large yellow slogan appears at the top.
visual_base.text_narrative_log: (1) [Slogan]: 訂閱挺健康 掌握健康指南. [Variety]: 6000年前的口膠!. (2) [Subtitle]: 丹麥哥本哈根大學與英國約克大學的團隊最近撿了古人嚼過的「口香糖」. (3) [Logo]: PROCEEDINGS B. [Slogan]: Research: Ancient DNA and biomarkers from archaeological artifacts. (4) [Subtitle]: 結果一驗發現這些新石器時代的人不但愛嚼東西還在焦油裡留下了性別飲食甚至工作分工的線索. (5) [Variety]: 6000年前的口膠!. (6) [Subtitle]: 故事要從一種叫「樺樹焦油」(birch tar)的黑色黏膠說起. (7) [Subtitle]: 不是猛毒而是黑玉斷續膏是最古老的「合成材料」. (8) [Subtitle]: 大約六千年前就被拿來黏石器、修陶罐. (9) [Subtitle]: 但這次厲害了考古學家從阿爾卑斯山周邊九個遺址挖出30件焦油樣本使出雙刀流來分析. (10) [Subtitle]: 第一刀是「有機殘留分析」透過氣相層析質譜儀(GC-MS)看成分. (11) [Subtitle]: 發現不少樣本混了松樹樹脂來調整黏性. (12) [Subtitle]: 而且修補陶器的焦油上還出現大量的「雙重降解標記」白話文就是「反覆加熱烤了又烤」. (13) [Subtitle]: 代表破罐補好繼續用恁省儉(an` sang` kiam). (14) [Subtitle]: 第二刀就是當紅的「古代DNA」(aDNA)分析. (15) [Subtitle]: 在12件有明顯牙齒印的「口香糖塊」也就是咀嚼焦油裡他們發現了海量的「人類口腔微生物」DNA. (16) [Subtitle]: 中位數30% 最高73% 甚至有幾塊被好幾個人咬過感情真好. (17) [Subtitle]: 除了口腔微生物他們從口香糖裡還找到了馴化的小麥、大麥野生的榛果、亞麻籽跟嗯罌粟籽. (18) [Variety]: Tight tight tight. (19) [Subtitle]: 再來他們從黏在「箭頭」上的焦油比對出了野豬跟淡水魚像狗魚和鯉魚的DNA. (20) [Subtitle]: 證明了這箭頭真的有拿去插過至於創造出幾位替身使者這就難說. (21) [Subtitle]: 最後從陶罐上用來修補的焦油他們發現黏著綿羊跟豌豆的DNA. (22) [Subtitle]: 這就暗示了這個罐子很可能拿來煮豆燉羊肉. (23) [Subtitle]: 你看光是DNA就把「飲食、狩獵、烹飪」三大場景全部還原邏輯非常清楚. (24) [Subtitle]: 蛤 你說廚餘呢廚餘拿去養豬了嗎有蒸煮過嗎臺中市都不知道了誰知道呢. (25) [Subtitle]: 還有一個發現值得注意在16個成功定序的樣本中. (26) [Subtitle]: 所有用來「黏工具黏武器」的焦油(共4個)通通是「男生」的DNA. (27) [Subtitle]: 而所有用來「補陶罐」的(共3個)通通是「女生」的DNA. (28) [Subtitle]: 當然這樣本數太少不能就此對性別分工下定論但這研究還是很厲害. (29) [Subtitle]: 畢竟那個年代留下的遺骸很少這些被咬過的焦油成了意想不到的DNA寶箱. (30) [Subtitle]: 以後交朋友記得要找能嚼同一片口香糖的不願意的通通絕交.
